title: Ballade no. 1 in G minor
source_citations: James Parakilas, Ballads Without Words: Chopin and the Tradition of the Instrumental Ballade (1992)
Edward Aldwell & Carl Schachter, Harmony and Voice Leading (analysis of Op. 23)
John Rink, Chopin: The Piano Concertos and Ballades (multiple references)

key_plan.role: Largo introduction in Neapolitan area (Ab–C minor inflection), unison declamation
Moderato; first theme in G minor — narrative-arched main idea
Lyrical second theme in relative major — chordal, hymn-like
Theme B continuation; passes through A minor and other keys before development
Development of theme A through A minor, F minor; brilliant figuration
Theme A returns in A minor (reversed key relationship vs. exposition) — Chopin's structural reversal
Theme B returns briefly in Eb major (the exposition key, not tonic)
Presto con fuoco — virtuosic coda returning to G minor; famous double-octave passages

notable_cadences.basis: Half cadence closing introduction, prepares G-minor main theme
Cadence closing theme B's first statement
Cadence closing the reversed-key recap of theme A

characteristic_features: First piano ballade — established the genre
Sonata-form modification: themes return in reversed key relationship in the recap (theme A in A minor instead of tonic, theme B in Eb instead of tonic)
Presto con fuoco coda is one of the most technically demanding passages in the 19th-century piano repertoire
Famous opening Neapolitan-flavored introduction has been the subject of extensive harmonic debate
common_omr_pitfalls: Wide-range piano writing — OMR voice splitting between hands often misassigns notes
Tempo rubato implied notation (small note values within larger metric pulses) creates rhythm-fragility issues
The Presto coda has very dense 32nd-note figuration that strains YOLO notehead detection
_notes: Curated 2026-05-24. The reversed key recap (A minor for theme A, Eb major for theme B) is the structurally most distinctive feature and gives the cross-check strong differentiating signal. Time signature varies between 6/4 (opening) and 2/2 (Presto coda) in some editions.
